unique_value: policy decision authority is separated from side-effect execution authority so neither plane can act alone
short-lived grants are cryptographically bound to the exact policy decision fingerprint and input digest
execution is fail-closed on policy refusal missing or invalid grants expiry decision drift input drift effect-scope expansion and replay
successful and refused executions produce deterministic receipts while a shared hash-chained audit log detects in-place history tampering
multi-principal quorum requires distinct principals and required roles rather than counting duplicate signatures
effect authority can attenuate through policy principal approval and grant stages but cannot expand
signer signatures are reverified and current provider confirmations are reconciled before quorum issuance

lineage_distinction.GlacierEQ/lockheed-evidence-binding-gate: binds external actions to content-addressed evidence snapshots; complementary evidence provenance, not actuator authority
lineage_distinction.GlacierEQ/lockheed-mission-thread-isolat: isolates mutable authority between mission threads; complementary isolation boundary, not dual-key side-effect authorization

capability_contribution.ownership: This repository remains the owning Lockheed-specialist implementation of dual-control side-effect authority; capability extraction preserves repository identity and lineage.

next_evolution: Add externally attested hardware provenance and signer/key revocation freshness, persist quorum/provider state safely across restart, and reconcile execution with an external side-effect provider confirmation without weakening exact decision/input/effect binding or single-use semantics.
nonclaims: no Lockheed Martin internal architecture claim
repository relationships do not imply exercised integration
hardware_backed is configured provider metadata and not independent physical hardware attestation
provider confirmation reconciliation currently covers signer authorization rather than external side-effect confirmation
quorum/provider state is not restart-safe or distributed
